1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. The exam at a glance. The five domains. How to answer every question. A four-week study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Exam overview, domain map and answer technique (all domains). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. Passing score. seven hundred or greater on a scale of one to one thousand. Time. one hundred minutes (a request for thirty extra minutes is possible if the exam is not in your preferred language). Format. Proctored; may include interactive components. Content. Most questions cover generally available features; preview features can appear if commonly used. Questions. The official pages do not state the number. Retake. After twenty-four hours for the first retake. Audience. Azure administrators with experience in compute, storage, networking and identity.

1.title: The exam at a glance, continued
1.text: The exam at a glance. Azure Active Directory (Azure A D) is now Microsoft Entra I D. The study guide already uses the new name. Exam tip: Expect scenario questions ("which option meets the requirement with the least administrative effort") and portal or command choices. Learn what each feature is for and which scope it applies at.

1.title: The five domains
1.text: The five domains. The figure shows this: Domain map: five domains and the modules that cover them.

1.title: The five domains, continued
1.text: The five domains. one. Manage Azure identities and governance. twenty-twenty-five percent. two. Implement and manage storage. fifteen-twenty percent. three. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. twenty-twenty-five percent. four. Implement and manage virtual networking. fifteen-twenty percent. five. Monitor and maintain Azure resources. ten-fifteen percent. Exam tip: Identities (twenty-twenty-five percent) plus compute (twenty-twenty-five percent) is up to half the exam. Monitoring is the smallest domain, but it is easy marks if you study it.

1.title: How to answer every question
1.text: How to answer every question. Read the last line to see what is asked. Underline the requirement: least administrative effort, lowest cost, no downtime, most secure. Eliminate options that use the wrong scope or the wrong service. Choose the built-in Azure feature designed for the job. Answer every question; there is no penalty stated for a wrong answer. Administrator habits: prefer managed identities to stored credentials, R B A C to sharing keys, private endpoints to public exposure, and policy to manual checks.

1.title: A four-week study plan
1.text: A four-week study plan. one. Modules: one to three. Goal: Identities, R B A C, governance. two. Modules: four to six. Goal: Storage. three. Modules: seven to eleven. Goal: A R M (Azure Resource Manager) and Bicep, virtual machines, containers, App Service. four. Modules: twelve to seventeen. Goal: Networking, monitoring, backup, mixed practice.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. What score is needed to pass the A Z-one hundred four exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: seven hundred. A score of seven hundred or greater out of one thousand is required.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. What was Azure Active Directory renamed to? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Microsoft Entra I D. Azure A D is now Microsoft Entra I D.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which two domains together can account for up to half of the exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Identities and governance, and compute. Each of those two domains is twenty to twenty-five percent.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A question asks for the option with the least administrative effort. What should the candidate choose? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A built-in managed Azure feature that meets the requirement. Managed features usually minimize administrative effort.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the passing score? Answer: seven hundred or greater out of one thousand. Question two. How long is the exam? Answer: one hundred minutes. Question three. Name the five domains. Answer: Identities and governance; storage; compute; virtual networking; monitoring and maintenance.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which domain is the smallest? Answer: Monitor and maintain Azure resources (ten to fifteen percent). Question five. What is the old name of Microsoft Entra I D? Answer: Azure Active Directory. Question six. After how long can a first retake be taken? Answer: After twenty-four hours.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: seven hundred to pass, one hundred minutes, proctored, interactive components possible. Domains: twenty to twenty-five or fifteen to twenty or twenty to twenty-five or fifteen to twenty or ten to fifteen percent. Old name: Azure A D equals Microsoft Entra I D. Method: read the last line, find the requirement, eliminate, choose the built-in feature.
